about: Every source gaba_excites takes a number, an equation or a method from, and what it took. The single source of truth: lit/README.md, lit/references.bib and public/lit.html are rendered from this file by `node scripts/lit.ts`, and src/lit.test.ts fails if they drift.

sources.title: Minimal Hodgkin–Huxley type models for different classes of cortical and thalamic neurons
sources.took: The regular-spiking pyramidal cell, the fast-spiking interneuron and the low-threshold-spike (LTS) pyramidal cell: their currents (Traub INa and IKd, slow IM; for the LTS cell, a T-type Ca²⁺ current and a calcium shell) and the published cells they make.

sources.title: ModelDB 123623: minimal Hodgkin–Huxley models of cortical and thalamic neurons (NEURON code for Pospischil et al. 2008)
sources.took: Every pyramidal-cell parameter, from sPY_template; every fast-spiking-cell parameter, from sIN_template; every LTS-cell parameter, from sPYr_template with demo_PY_LTS.hoc's settings; with HH_traub.mod, IM_cortex.mod, IT_huguenard.mod and cadecay_destexhe.mod — and the mechanisms themselves, run in NEURON as the oracle each port is tested against.

sources.title: LTS cells in cerebral cortex and their role in generating spike-and-wave oscillations
sources.took: Credited as the original of the LTS cell, which sPYr_template says it is taken from. No number is read from the paper: every value is ModelDB 123623's code.

sources.title: Simulation of the currents involved in rhythmic oscillations in thalamic relay neurons
sources.took: Credited as the source of the T-type Ca²⁺ current's kinetics, as IT_huguenard.mod cites it. The equations used are the .mod file's, transcribed in the note; they have not been checked against the paper's text.

sources.title: A novel T-type current underlies prolonged Ca(2+)-dependent burst firing in GABAergic neurons of rat thalamic reticular nucleus
sources.took: Credited because IT_huguenard.mod names it beside Huguenard & McCormick 1992 as the data its T current is based on. Nothing is read from it here.

sources.title: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neuron excitability is regulated by estradiol feedback and kisspeptin
sources.took: The GnRH neuron: Equations 1–24, Tables 1–3 (negative-feedback parameter set), Cm = 20 pF and I_app = −6 pA, and the two published numbers the port is checked against — rest at −70 mV and the Fig. 7F spike counts.

quotes.text: I app is the applied current, which was set to −6 pA to hold the cell at −70 mV.
cells were injected with current from 0 to 30 pA (500 ms, 2 pA steps)
Current injections were initiated from a mean membrane potential of −69 ± 2 mV, near the value determined in the above experiments.
quotes.where: Results; the earlier experiments are on-cell measurements of Vm

quotes.text: This was positive relative to the resting potential (−50.7 ± 1.7 mV, from current-clamp measurements)

sources.title: Response of gonadotropin-releasing hormone neurons from female mice to dynamic-clamp-simulated GABAergic conductances across development and after prenatal androgenization
sources.took: The GnRH cell's default GABA PSC: decay τ 10 ms (9.9 ± 0.25 ms in adult females), peak ≈ 1 nS (≈ −30 pA at −70 mV, Fig. 2B read by eye), instantaneous rise as in their dynamic clamp. Best available rather than ground truth: decay τ depends on chloride, and intracellular chloride in GnRH neurons was never measured directly.

quotes.text: The decay time constant of GABAergic PSCs is strongly dependent on the concentration of chloride in the recording pipette.
quotes.where: Methods 2.5, Properties of isolated GABAergic PSCs in GnRH neurons

quotes.text: an age‐dependent increase in decay time constant from 7.4 ± 0.1 ms to 9.9 ± 0.2 ms was detected
quotes.where: Methods 2.6, Modelling of the GABAergic postsynaptic conductances

quotes.text: a range of conductances within and moderately above the physiological range of GABA PSCs was used (1, 2, 5, 10 nS)

sources.title: Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) neuron potassium currents and excitability in both sexes exhibit minimal changes upon removal of negative feedback
sources.took: Not used in the app. The slowly inactivating K⁺ current's inactivation (V½ ≈ −30 mV, slope ≈ 4.7, τ of seconds to tens of seconds) was added to the GnRH model's I_K in an experiment, to ask what it would do: at the published V½, nothing measurable.

quotes.text: full inactivation and recovery required >10s at +50 and −100 mV, respectively.
quotes.where: Materials and Methods, Voltage-gated potassium current characterization

quotes.text: Because inactivation was incomplete even after 51.29 s at −30 mV, this remaining current was not subtracted and the inactivation graphs level off at ∼30%.
quotes.where: Materials and Methods, Activation and inactivation of the slow current

sources.title: Estradiol feedback alters potassium currents and firing properties of gonadotropin-releasing hormone neurons
sources.access: not in hand (on the owner's want-list)
sources.took: The 1 V/s dV/dt criterion for GnRH action-potential threshold, which the owner defined in this paper. The notebook's report tabulates threshold at 1 V/s alongside 2, 10 and 20 V/s. Also the report that estradiol lowers GnRH threshold and latency through I_A, which motivated the K⁺-block experiments. Attributed on the owner's word (2026-10-18); the PDF has not been read here, so there is no quotation yet.

sources.title: Axonal sodium channel distribution shapes the depolarized action potential threshold of dentate granule neurons
sources.took: The 10 V/s threshold criterion, tabulated in the notebook's report. Also the comparison the threshold experiments reproduce: intracellular TEA, with a bias current restoring a negative rest, left voltage threshold unchanged and changed rheobase.

quotes.text: The membrane potential at which phase plot slope reached 10 mV ms-1 (Kress et al., 2008; Naundorf et al., 2006; Shu et al., 2007) was denoted voltage threshold.
Blocking DG neuron KVs with intracellular TEA depolarized the resting membrane potential and altered rheobase but did not alter action potential voltage threshold.
It is possible that subthreshold potassium currents, especially those on the axon, might participate in setting voltage threshold (Bekkers and Delaney, 2001; Shah et al., 2008).

sources.title: Excitability and burst generation of AVPV kisspeptin neurons are regulated by the estrous cycle via multiple conductances modulated by estradiol action
sources.took: The 2 V/s dV/dt criterion for action-potential threshold, which the notebook's report tabulates alongside 1, 10 and 20 V/s. The owner remembered it as the lab's KNDy convention, from Luhong Wang's recordings; the paper's cells are AVPV kisspeptin neurons, and it measures threshold at rheobase from −70 mV, as the app does.

quotes.text: The action potential threshold was defined as the membrane potential at which the derivative exceeded 2 V/s.

sources.title: Norepinephrine suppresses gonadotropin-releasing hormone neuron excitability in the adult mouse
sources.took: GnRH neuron resting potentials by gramicidin perforated patch, by sex and cycle stage (−55.5 to −59.4 mV): evidence for the GABA opening's resting potential near −60 mV.

quotes.text: Under perforated-patch, resting membrane potentials (RMP; mV) were -59.4±1.0 (males, N=39), -55.5±1.5 (diestrous females, N=11), -59.3±1.2 (proestrous females, N=14), -55.6±2.5 (estrous females, N=13) and -58.8±1.1 (OVX females, N=11).

sources.title: Kisspeptin excites gonadotropin-releasing hormone neurons through a phospholipase C/calcium-dependent pathway regulating multiple ion channels
sources.took: GnRH neuron resting potential by gramicidin perforated patch, −55 ± 1 mV (n = 188), junction potential not corrected (~−2 mV).

quotes.text: The 188 GnRH neurons included in this report had an average resting membrane potential (RMP) of -55±1mV and Rin of 1478±35MOhms.

sources.title: Identified GnRH neuron electrophysiology: a decade of study
sources.took: The range of GnRH neuron interspike potentials (−65 to −50 mV, whole-cell or perforated patch) against the on-cell estimate (~−75 mV).

quotes.text: The interspike potential of the majority of GnRH neurons is between −65 and −50 mV recorded in either whole-cell or perforated-patch configuration
Measurements made using a non-invasive method suggested a more hyperpolarized membrane potential of ~−75 mV.

sources.title: Potassium-coupled chloride cotransport controls intracellular chloride in rat neocortical pyramidal neurons
sources.took: Not used in the app. Its outside-out patch calibrations (pipette Cl⁻ known; 40 mM read off Fig. 2A) and solution recipes, refitted in an experiment to ask what the paper's one-sided activity factor was absorbing: a voltage error of about 6 mV (about half the Henderson junction potential) plus a small permeant pipette anion.

quotes.text: [Cl−]o was set to the extracellular Cl− concentration, corrected for activity (Robinson and Stokes, 1959) (e.g., in 3.5 mM [K+]o, 139.6 mM × 76% = 106.1 mM).
quotes.where: Materials and Methods, Intracellular chloride calculation

quotes.text: Liquid junction potentials for all solutions were measured, and all voltages reported are corrected values (Neher, 1992).
Our results with excised patches demonstrated an effective concentration of pipette Cl− of 2.06 ± 0.16 mM when only 1 mM KCl was added.
quotes.where: Materials and Methods, The role of bicarbonate and other anions

sources.title: Liquid junction potentials and small cell effects in patch-clamp analysis
sources.took: The generalized Henderson equation for a liquid junction potential, and its sign convention (true Vm = V_read − LJP). Used only in an experiment.

sources.title: JPCalc, a software package for calculating liquid junction potential corrections in patch-clamp, intracellular, epithelial and bilayer measurements and for correcting junction potential measurements
sources.took: Relative ion mobilities (K⁺ = 1; Na⁺ 0.682, Cl⁻ 1.0388, gluconate 0.33, HCO3⁻ 0.605, Ca²⁺ 0.4048, Mg²⁺ 0.361), for the Henderson equation. Used only in an experiment.
